answer: Register one timber hall per applicant. A warden photographs a numbered beam and sets a pearl in a raven weathervane's eye. Monthly the keeper logs a dawn photo, and a neighbor signs it. Twice a season the warden checks the pearl against the intake photo and reads the log against weather notes. A forged hall loses its 150 token deposit, and its applicant is barred 180 days. Faking 10,000 halls freezes 1,500,000 tokens and costs 950,000 dollars. Like a barn pegged true at each joint, an identity of timber, pearl, and raven holds while it can be checked, and a fake one falls on first check.
